summary: A backfill step clears orphan referrer_id values, the new Saleor version is deployed with a state‑only migration, the old version is retired, and finally a foreign‑key constraint from account_user.referrer_id to account_user.id is added, giving the column a proper self‑reference while keeping both versions correct during the overlap.
write_consistency: During the overlap a backfill stage sets referrer_id to NULL for any row whose value does not reference an existing account_user id, preventing constraint violations. The foreign‑key constraint is added only after retire_old, when the old version no longer writes to the column, so the new version can safely enforce the FK without breaking the old code.

stages.description: Set referrer_id to NULL for rows where the value is not a valid account_user primary key.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM account_user u WHERE u.id = account_user.referrer_id);

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this only the new version serves traffic.
Add a foreign‑key constraint from account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user.id, completing the schema change.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
